Health geography of Portuguese freguesias, both vintages

Source: R/data.R
pt_health_codes.Rd

One row per freguesia per health vintage. Keyed on the freguesia rather than the município because unit varies within a município in five of them — the reason this cannot live alongside pt_nuts_codes, which is município grained.

Usage

pt_health_codes

Format

A data.frame with 6518 rows and columns:

health_vintage

"2022" or "2024".

dtmnfr

6-digit freguesia code, current vintage.

reg_saude

Região de saúde (2024) or the former ARS (2022).

scheme

"uls" for 2024, "aces" for 2022 — different concepts, not two names for one thing.

unit

The local unit: a ULS or an ACES.

unit_municipio

Município-grained approximation of unit.

Source

Decreto-Lei 102/2023 (ULS); prior ARS/ACES organization.

Details

Mappings are recorded against the current (2025) freguesia set; pt_lookup() reaches them from an earlier admin_vintage.

Vintages

"2024"

The reform: 5 regiões de saúde on the mainland plus the island services, and ULS (Unidades Locais de Saúde) as the local unit.

"2022"

What it superseded: the former ARS, and ACES (Agrupamentos de Centros de Saúde) as the local unit.

unit_municipio is the unit to use for data by município. Units that share a município are merged into one pseudo-unit, and merging follows chains, so it can differ from unit even in a município that lies whole in one unit. For example, ULS São José also covers part of Loures, which merges ULS Loures-Odivelas with Lisboa's three ULS, and Odivelas gets the merged unit too. Everywhere else it equals unit.

See also

pt_lookup(), pt_registry

Examples

table(pt_health_codes$health_vintage, pt_health_codes$scheme)
#>       
#>        aces  uls
#>   2022 3259    0
#>   2024    0 3259
